tips.comment: Diego Ventura won a listed race in Paris after finishing 3rd place at Newmarket behind Cosmic Year, who ran well in the Irish 2000 Guineas. I think he is the one to beat.

The Charlie Appleby runner will have to bounce back from two below-par runs at Meydan and Ascot. Although his last run over an inadequate 6f wasn't too bad considering it was a Group 3 race. The slight ease in the ground shouldn't bother the Godolphin runner, and it shouldn't be forgotten he beat the subsequent French Derby winner last September at Doncaster.

You can argue The Waco Kid nicked the race when beating Diego Ventura to win the Group 3 Tattersalls Stakes at Newmarket last September. He does carry a penalty for that win, but he beat today's favorite by 2.25L that day. 2lbs worse off here, but he's 3lbs clear on ratings, and there doesn't look to be loads of pace on offer. Stall 3 at this tight turning track means he could grab the rail and go in first-time cheekpieces. With cut in the ground, he could be really hard to peg back.

Andrew Balding's filly looked progressive when winning at Newmarket's Guineas meeting, recording a personal best. Her third in a hot handicap at York's Ebor meeting has worked out well, and I shouldn't think a 4lb rise for her last win will stop the 4yo.

7f at Epsom has a small bias for the low stalls and a more pronounced bias for being a front runner. 3rd best track in the country for front runners over the 7f. To my eye, there's only two real front runners in here: Partisan Hero and Legal Reform. Legal Reform, as an 8yo with the highest OR he's ever had, can't possibly be a bet really, so it only leaves the one. 5yo, so has a maturity advantage over some of these, hasn't been out of the first 3 since May 24 and ran his best race to date when 2nd behind Two Tempting at Chester. Had to cover more ground than the winner there and was only beaten in the last couple strides to finish 0.75L behind. That was 7.5f, so the drop to 7f may suit even more. Up 3lbs as a result of the last day, however, with conditions to suit, should really be in the places if producing a repeat.

This horse is friendless in the early market but looks terrific value to me with Hollie Doyle booked for the first time. She replaces a jockey with really poor stats who has been on board for all 3 runs since the stable brought in the horse. As a result, the horse has slipped down to a career-low mark now of just 87. A look at his dead heat 2nd in a maiden at Naas last year is all the evidence we need that he's much better than that. Both the winner and the dead heat 2nd have won when rated 104 since, so Majestic Wave will surely be competitive here off a 17lb lower mark.

Havana Hurricane was a bargain buy at 9k Guineas compared to the Breeze Up purchase Maximized, which cost £650k. Both impressed with their respective wins first time out. However, the 7-2 available about Havana Hurricane is better value as he coped well with the contours of Goodwood over 5f, doing his best work at the finish. He should appreciate the extra furlong at Epsom, and with a better start than last time, he could make use of his inside draw to grab the rail round the bend.

The 2yo was well supported when winning on his debut during March, a 17 runner £21K novice stakes and seems well regarded in the yard. Plenty to like how he picked up 2f out and saw the race out - maybe not the best track position that day. The forecast rain on Thursday will be a plus. He comes here fresh for this conditions race after 11 weeks off the track and you could expect plenty more improvement.

Botanical has been running well in defeat in Listed races and has been dropped a couple of pounds by the handicapper. Epsom is a track where top weights do well due to the undulating, turning nature of the track and horses can never get up to top speeds. With Ryan Moore booked you would hope he has a great chance.

Roger Varian has a strong record in this race, having won it 4 times since 2014. He has another good chance this year with Defiance who ran really well behind Bellum Justum in a Derby trial here on reappearance last year, going down 0.75L when conceding first run. Hung badly next time when down the field at Lingfield and then clearly not right at Royal Ascot in the Group 2 KE VII Stakes. Off since but makes his handicap debut from a mark of 99 which on a line through Bellum Justum - now rated 112 after winning a couple of Group races - leaves him really well handicapped at a track he clearly handles well. Ground should be fine and he went well fresh here last year. Looks an obvious blot if ready to go first time.

Going to get this one in early. Backed this on debut last year at 150-1 and it won (and on here I believe) as well as an EW Lucky-15, which pretty much set me up for the year. Has been very consistent ever since, the last three over 1m, but looks more suited, in my opinion, to further and has run well over 1m4f. This race will also be fine (1m 2f) as she is better when coming late and will not mind any rain and change in the going. Trainer has had 3 runners at Epsom with a record of 2nd, 3rd, and 4th, so not bad and makes this one a decent EW play.

21 runs, 3 wins and 10 placed efforts tells us Rathgar is pretty consistent and gets in here at the foot of the weights bar one. He seems to cope with quirky tracks if I can call Chester, Goodwood and here at Epsom quirky. Also versatile regarding underfoot conditions so everything is in place for a bold show.

The 4yo is on top of his game, three runs this year, going close each time, all on the AW. He was 2nd of 14 last time out, beaten just a nse in a useful £34K handicap, and comes here fresh after a seven week break. Facing some stronger rivals in this handicap but he’s on a nice looking mark. The return to turf might give him a little spark, a couple of decent runs as a youngster in Group company on turf. Not a great draw but is worth an EW shout.

‘Desert Flower’ is the short-price favorite for the ‘Oaks’ classic, but I’ll take a chance on the unexposed selection at a better price. He was only 2L behind that runner in the recent 1000 Guineas, which was just his second career start and a first run after an 8-month break. Any improvement would put him in the mix. There are question marks about the 12f trip for the favorite, while the well-bred selection shouldn’t have any problems.

The 5yo progressed nicely last year. Decent run on his return during March in the 22 runner £77K Lincoln handicap - poor draw that day. He’s been kept fresh for this £38K handicap with a 10 week break. Just one previous run at this tricky track, a close 2nd over this C/D as a youngster. He’s on a decent mark, the forecast rain, low draw and strong jockey booking are all positives.

Last year's winner Two Tempting is very tempting but is in a much stiffer mark here and will do well to fend off some unexposed sorts here. The one I like most is this one who won over C&D last time and looks most progressive. Half brother to the tip top Grade 1 winner Bradsell and must have more to come. Has placed form on softish ground but dam was a 7f Listed winner on heavy ground so there is a good chance this one will relish conditions and is already proven at the track. Early booking at a low weight of Hollie Doyle knocked my eye out earlier in the week and the 12-1 voucher is burning a hole in my proverbial pocket now! Still looks value as has so much in his favour. Big shout from fair draw.

Decent form from the 4yo last year. He didn’t do a lot wrong two weeks ago, after coming off an 8 month break, and should be better for the run - he was up against some consistent race fit rivals that day. Slightly lower mark now and is running in calmer waters.

Guy Fawkes's form on paper may be slightly off putting however looks can be deceiving and a much deeper analysis of this individual tells a whole different story was last seen at Redcar 36 days ago where finishing a never nearer 8th/10 however his mark continues to rapidly ease and he is now operating on an extremely dangerous mark of 57 in a race that is up to his level and Guy Fawkes's is a horse that does have potential he just needs things to drop right and a good analysis of this class 6 handicap clearly shows this race is well in his favour jockey D Tudhope takes the ride and can give Charlie Clover's Gelded son of Harry Angel & Fire Blaze ( Dam's sire Dubawi ) a promising ride here at Thirsk a worth noting jockey D Tudhope has a 22% strike rate here at Thirsk that statistic being much better than it looks given the odds involved currently off the handicapper's radar for the time being it would be a wise and profitable move to catch him running well at this stage must be taken extremely seriously in a race of this nature . Respected .

A big improvement from the 4yo last week, after coming back from a 7 month break. He won a 10 runner handicap by 6L, earning a huge RPR rating. Higher mark for this handicap but still 2lb lower than his opening mark four runs back. Due to be racing off a 7lb higher mark in future races and he looks a nice bet.

Two of the stable's last five runners have won when booking this jockey at 10/1 and 28/1, and this outsider looks to have every chance on the book too. The horse is well-bred, and the owners show a very nice profit if you backed all their runners for this trainer blindly. The placed effort in a hot 19-runner handicap at York a year ago gave a glimpse of what this horse is capable of, and he could be even better in his 4-year-old campaign now. The run last time out would have blown away the cobwebs, and he's only 2lb above his last winning mark now. The jockey booking also looks significant since he's won once from just two rides on the horse.
Green Impact disappointed in the 2000 Guineas at Newmarket but went there without a run and probably needed the race. He looks the class horse in this Listed event.
Has good French form, is a very strong finisher, is well weighted on return. Yard has a 20% win rate at this race in the past.

Going to take a chance on Eastwatch here, who looked very impressive last time out in the first 3-year-old race to back up the decent 3rd in the only 2-year-old race. That 2-year-old race has worked out well, and although this is another pick today thrown in at the deep end, this one could also cope in my opinion and could surprise.

At a massive price, I'm going to chance this J Nallen runner, Cristal Clere, which goes up in distance. With the trainer not coming here for nothing, normally with 3 from 6 wins, he must think something of it in this Listed contest. E/W.

IMPRESSIVE winner last time. Not sure what he beat, but he forged clear from 2f out, looking better the further he went. Steps up in class, which he deserves the chance, and over this longer trip, which should suit.

SOUND OF LIGHTNING has won a race at 1m. A winner on her latest outing over 1m at Naas last month. Upped in trip to 1m 1f should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to go in again and win this race.

ECHINACEA is a likely improver up in trip with stamina on her dam side. That should serve her well ahead of her handicap debut today and the market appears to have overlooked this three year old filly taking on her own age group feasibly treated for this sphere of racing.

Going nap on another Jessica Harrington runner here with Shane Foley on board. Instant Appeal, who is lightly raced for a four-year-old, ran well enough when third last time at Naas. If improving on that run, he could certainly be involved in the finish here tonight.

Another wide-open Irish handicap with 18 runners, and I always think you need a bit of luck at this track. This has won its last two races, last time out over jumps, but the race before was on the flat over further. It is drawn well in 1, and as long as not boxed in like the last run over course and distance in March, it has decent each-way chances and could easily win, getting weight off all. (each way for betting)
Scored over this distance at Tipperary last year; found 1m6f too demanding at Gowran on season return - should be sharper now back at ideal trip.

As mentioned in my win tip, a wide-open race and this trainer/jockey combo got me a nice 35-1 shot winner yesterday. So, I will take a chance with Solomon to spring back into life after four poor efforts (last three not pro jockeys) since coming to Ireland. Mark is now down to 82, so we might see improvement now. I also like Pink Socks, but it's a seasonal debut, and Thatwilldoso, which I was going to pick as my each-way tip, but this site has the odds wrong, so I left it. (Also strange that 365 have it at 9's with others at 28 & 25's, so it might also be a nice each-way.)

Unterberg is still a maiden after 13 starts on turf, but he has twice finished second in Cork handicaps. The first time was over 9 furlongs last August, and he repeated that when beaten by 1 length there last month. He is off the same mark here and must have a good each-way chance with 5 places on offer.

Rampage has been a bit unlucky with his draws here the last two times, and although still not great today, it's a lot better. He hasn't won for a while but is a C & D winner and is due a change of luck.

Strong each-way bet on this one. Wiley Harrington has seen to it that this one has been ridden with handicaps in mind. Not given a hard time on two handicaps to date. Drops to 62 here, and this could well be a target race.

Moonhall Lass showed her best form of the year with a strong third in a big field recently. Dropping down 2 pounds now and with an additional 3-pound jockey claimer, she looks well placed to be involved again. Definitely an each-way chance.

Wasn't beaten far when finishing third over 1m 2f at Ballinrobe last month but was well beaten when dropped back to 7f at Down Royal six days ago. Step up in trip should suit. Has won one and placed in two of his six starts since joining this yard at the end of March. Jamie Powell's 3lb claim should come in useful. Good EW bet.
Johnny Murtagh sticks on the cheekpiece here on Amber Blossom, which may have a positive effect. It's on a good mark for this and looks a lively outsider.

RISING SKY has had a look at handicap company latest and her effort hinted she may be best suited by tonight's step up to the mile trip. She was not knocked around in that race and has been dropped 3lb in the handicap which seems generous. She could be the three year old seen to be st effect taking on her own age group.

Trainer John Joseph Murphy has a good chance here with The Dark Baron, who finished down the field under an extremely restrained ride over six furlongs at Roscommon when making his handicap debut last month. Today, he gets in here off a three lb lower and steps up to a mile for the first time, which should help, as should a more positive ride from stable jockey Joey Sheridan.

I wasn’t planning to get involved in this contest, but a good friend & fellow tipster had me take a second look - and from a price perspective alone, WIDELY ACCLAIMED looks far too tempting to ignore at current odds of 20/1. This 3-year-old colt, trained by Ado McGuinness, was only a length behind MOONHALL LASS - today’s shorter-priced rival - just 24 days ago at Roscommon (7½f, Good), where the latter was backed into favouritism.
A Son of ACLAIM, WIDELY ACCLAIMED finished a staying-on 5th that day and now drops 3lbs in the weights, which could prove key. He steps up slightly in trip here, and that move looks a positive on the back of his closing effort last time out.
McGuinness might have only the one recent winner, but he boasts an impressive 38.89% strike rate for runners hitting the frame in the past fortnight. Retained rider Adam Caffrey - who knows this horse well - has a solid 30.77% place strike rate for the yard over the past year.
Given the form lines, weight drop, and encouraging trainer/jockey stats, I’d be kicking myself if I didn’t have at least a small play at these odds.

Forty Kay is a 5-year-old daughter of No Risk at All ex Calakanga, who traces back to two great broodmares, namely Sweet Mimosa by Le Levanstell and Feemoss by Ballymoss. She makes her racecourse debut here in this bumper, where she'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins, in the colors of the Blueblood Racing Club. She receives 7 lbs sex allowance and this may tip it in her favor. I make my selection my Nap of the day.
